question: What does this repository appear to be for, based only on the HEAD tree, README, and commit record in the pack?
Classify it as one of: service, library, script, infra, docs, experiment, husk, unknown. Say why in one sentence.
At HEAD, is there product code that could run or be imported, or only docs, comments, config, and placeholders?
Do recent commits change behavior, or are they comments, markdown, whitespace, lockfile, or empty?
Does the README describe what is actually in the tree, or does it over-claim?
Is the record perpetual WIP without a coherent increment?
Is meaningful change coming from humans or from bots?
Are there ritual, duplicate-content, or comment-only commits that look like attendance?
What is the occupancy story: steady, fade, hot-potato, burst-then-graveyard, or one person?
Which coding assistants (Cursor, Copilot, Claude, Codex, Devin, Aider, …) appear in trailers, authors, or subjects? Is this human-directed edits or autonomous commit streams?
Does this look like a scaffolded demo or rewrite pitch sitting on top of (or instead of) a durable system — README claims replace/modernize/platform, tree is Vite/CRA defaults?
Is this run-the-business shared services (logging, security, on-call, IaC, CI) that other teams depend on, or a one-off demo?
Is the only artifact a requirements/spec markdown that never becomes working software?
Are they greenfielding a bespoke replacement for something that is normally bought as a suite? Cite README claims vs the tree.
Which up to 3 commit hashes from this pack should a human open first, and why?
